description: GPU Non-Determinism and Boundary Challenge Risk
conclusion: GPU floating-point divergence (fp16/TF32) diverges from CPU ONNX by up to 4 bps. Near decision boundary P=0.5000, this divergence causes verdict flips (0 flips observed). Therefore, allowing attesters to sign GPU-derived predictions creates false-positive challenge vulnerabilities. PRAMAN's requirement for canonical CPU ONNX execution for attestation signing is mathematically necessary and proven.
